digest.component_or_area: Lock management across enrichment, compaction, and GC workers
propositions: Three identical O_EXCL file lock implementations (enrich_drain, compact_trigger, gc_trigger) duplicate acquire/release logic with stamped_file_is_stale staleness checking, necessitating consolidation into a shared module.

The drain's release wraps close and unlink in a single try block, leaking the lock if close fails, while compact and GC use two independent tries ensuring unlink always runs—the shared implementation must adopt the two-block form as a behaviour fix.

The implementations differ in stamp bytes (drain appends newline, others do not), logging verbosity (drain names holder and warns on failure), and directory creation mechanisms (drain and compaction use makedirs, GC uses Path.mkdir), requiring callbacks and path-only contract for the helper.

Extract stamped_file_lock(path, label, describe_holder=None) and release_stamped_lock(path, fd) into src/rebar/_store/stamped_lock.py, keeping staleness logic in lock_owner.py and directory creation with the three callers.

The guard criterion os.O_CREAT AND stamped_file_is_stale (excluding stamped_lock.py itself) must match exactly the three current copies, survive seven unrelated O_EXCL uses, and never match doctor_locks, a read-only diagnostic tool.

Monkeypatched module-level attributes _acquire_trigger_lock and release_trigger_lock in compact_trigger must remain resolvable by name for test_lock_holder_labelling.py:134-135, and all six lock functions must preserve their public signatures and concurrent exclusion semantics.
